kaps_punt: Suid-Afrika het 'n besonder ryk fossielrekord van plante, diere en vroeë mense; belangrike fossiele wat in Suid-Afrika aangetref word, sluit in die Coelacanth en Afrikaanse dinosourusse; die "Wieg van die mensdom" is een van die plekke waar belangrike fossiele van die mensdom in Suid-Afrika gevind is

items.bewering: Mense het in ons land al baie fossiele van plante en van diere gevind. Hulle het ook fossiele van vroeë mense in die rotse gevind.
items.bron: Wits Evolutionary Studies Institute (wits.ac.za/esi): large, internationally acclaimed collections of dinosaurs, therapsids, plants and fossil hominids; UNESCO WHC 915 (Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa).

items.bewering: Ons land se fossielrekord is besonder ryk aan al drie hierdie groepe. Dit beteken daar is hier baie fossiele en ook baie soorte.
items.bron: South African Journal of Science 2025 review 'Taung and beyond' (sajs.co.za/article/view/18509): South Africa hosts the single richest early hominin fossil record worldwide; Karoo Supergroup outcrops long regarded as the largest and richest collecting grounds for therapsids (Wikipedia 'Karoo Supergroup', Iziko Karoo palaeontology collection); Wits ESI for plants and dinosaurs. 'Besonder ryk' is a comparative, not an absolute superlative, and holds for all three groups.

items.bewering: Hulle is boonop op baie verskillende plekke in ons land gevind.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915: hominin sites in Gauteng, North West (Taung) and Limpopo (Makapan); dinosaur trackways in the Free State and Eastern Cape (Daily Maverick 30 Jan 2020 on Golden Gate; SAJS 'Darting towards Storm Shelter'); Devonian fossils at Waterloo Farm near Makhanda (ScienceDaily 21 Sep 2015).

items.bewering: Al die fossiele van 'n land vorm saam sy fossielrekord.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters 'Fossil record' and encyclopedia.com 'Fossil': the fossil record is the totality of fossils and their occurrence in the rock strata. Applying it to one country is a fair narrowing.

items.bewering: Fossiele lê byna altyd in die lae van sedimentêre rots.
items.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
items.bron: Discover Magazine 'Why are fossils only found in sedimentary rocks?'; AMNH 'How do we know where to look for dinosaur fossils?'. 'Byna altyd' correctly leaves room for the rare exceptions (e.g. volcanic ash, amber).

items.bewering: Groot dele van ons land lê juis op sedimentêre rots. Die Karoo is een van daardie dele, en dit is 'n baie groot gebied.
items.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Karoo Supergroup' (citing the Council for Geoscience literature) and PSSA field guide (palaeosa.org): the mostly sedimentary Karoo Supergroup covers almost two-thirds of the land surface of southern Africa.

items.bewering: Ons land het dus baie van die regte soort rots waarin fossiele lê.
items.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
items.bron: Follows from the two items above (Karoo Supergroup extent; fossils preserved in sedimentary rock). The inference is sound.

items.bewering: Fossiele van dinosourusse uit Afrika is ook hier in ons land gevind.
items.bron: Wits WIReDSpace Massospondylus literature: Massospondylus is so abundant that it names the uppermost biozone of the Karoo Supergroup; first material found at Harrismith in 1853.

items.bewering: Hierdie dinosourusse het in Afrika geleef, lank voordat daar mense was.
items.bron: Elliot and Clarens Formation dinosaurs are Late Triassic to Early Jurassic (Wits WIReDSpace; Golden Gate trackways about 183 million years old, Daily Maverick 30 Jan 2020), against hominins of a few million years (UNESCO WHC 915).

items.bewering: Party van die fossiele is bene en tande wat in die rots bly lê het. Ander is spore wat 'n dier lank gelede in sagte modder getrap het.
items.bron: Bones: 56 Massospondylus bones from Harrismith (Wits literature). Trackways inside South Africa: Golden Gate area, Free State (Daily Maverick 2020, after Bordy et al., PLOS ONE); Mafube, Free State, over 80 tracks (PeerJ 2016, peerj.com/articles/2285); Storm Shelter, Eastern Cape (SAJS). Tracks are made in soft sediment that later hardens.

items.bewering: Wetenskaplikes het lank net fossiele van visse soos die Coelacanth geken. Hulle het nie verwag om so 'n vis lewend in die see te sien nie.
items.bron: Natural History Museum London, 'Coelacanths: the fish that outdid the Loch Ness monster'; History Today, 'Discovery of a living fossil': the group was known only from fossils and thought extinct for some 65-70 million years.

items.bewering: In 1938 is 'n lewende Coelacanth voor die kus van ons land gevang.
items.bron: Rhodes University news archive 2013 'Discovery of famous fish remembered'; SAHO: caught by trawler captain Hendrik Goosen off the Chalumna River mouth near East London, reported to Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer on 22 December 1938. It was caught alive and died soon after; 'lewende' is correct for the catch.

items.bewering: Die nuus daaroor het die hele wêreld verras.
items.bron: Natural History Museum London and History Today (as above): the find was an international sensation.

items.bewering: Die Coelacanth is 'n groot vis wat diep in die see lewe.
items.bron: FishBase summary 2063 (Latimeria chalumnae): depth range 150-700 m, usually 180-250 m; maximum length up to 2 m; NHM: the 1938 fish was 1.5 m long.

items.bewering: Die vis wat gevang is, lyk baie soos die diere in daardie fossiele. Hy wys dat 'n dier in 'n fossiel kan lyk soos 'n dier wat vandag lewe.
items.bron: NHM London and History Today: J.L.B. Smith identified it as a coelacanth because it matched the fossil forms. The comparison was checked as a mapping: it says 'lyk baie soos', not 'is dieselfde', and the block's last sentence names a different, extinct coelacanth, so a learner is not led to think the modern fish is a fossil species unchanged.

items.bewering: Naby Makhanda in die Oos-Kaap is ook fossiele van een ander soort Coelacanth in die rots gevind, 'n soort wat lank gelede uitgesterf het.
items.bron: ScienceDaily 21 Sep 2015 and Grocott's Mail (Rhodes University): Serenichthys kowiensis, a Late Devonian coelacanth of about 360 million years ago, described by Gess and Coates (Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society 2015) from black shale at Waterloo Farm near Makhanda (Grahamstown); more than 30 specimens.

items.bewering: Die Wieg van die Mensdom is 'n werklike plek in Gauteng.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915 and SAHO 'The Fossil Hominid Sites of Sterkfontein, Swartkrans, Kromdraai, and Environs': about 45 km west of Johannesburg. UNESCO says the Sterkfontein Valley landscape lies in both western Gauteng and North West; most of it is in Gauteng, so the statement is true as written, but not complete. 'Hoofsaaklik in Gauteng' would be the exact form if the writer wants it.

items.bewering: Dit is 'n gebied met baie grotte in 'n soort rots wat ons dolomiet noem.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915: dolomitic limestone ridges, most sites in caves; Stony Brook / Wits literature on the Sterkfontein Caves: hominin-bearing caves in karstified dolomite of the Malmani Subgroup.

items.bewering: Navorsers het in daardie grotte al baie fossiele van vroeë mense gevind.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915; Wikipedia 'Cradle of Humankind' (Sterkfontein alone produced more than a third of early hominid fossils found before 2010; over 1 500 Homo naledi specimens from the Dinaledi Chamber).

items.bewering: Die plek het sy naam gekry omdat soveel van hierdie fossiele juis daar gevind is.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915 / SAHO: the area 'is also called the Cradle of Humankind because it includes remains of hominids'; South African Tourism: the largest known concentration of human ancestral remains.

items.bewering: Dit is een van die plekke in ons land met sulke fossiele.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915: the 2005 extension added the Taung Skull Fossil Site and Makapan Valley, which lie outside the Cradle.

items.bewering: Die Wieg is vandag 'n Wêrelderfenisgebied, en die grotte word beskerm.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915: inscribed 1999 (now 'Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa'); SAHRA heritage reports: under the National Heritage Resources Act fossils and fossil sites may not be altered or destroyed.

items.bewering: Hierdie fossiele vertel ons watter plante en diere lank gelede hier geleef het. Hulle wys ook in watter dele van ons land vroeë mense geleef het.
items.bron: UNESCO WHC 915 (the sites have produced abundant information on human evolution over at least 3.5 million years); Wits ESI collections of fossil plants and animals.

items.bewering: Navorsers van regoor die wêreld kom hierheen om die fossiele te bestudeer.
items.bron: Wits ESI describes its collections as internationally acclaimed; the 2025 Sterkfontein dating was led by Darryl Granger's team (Purdue, USA), and the coelacanth work at Waterloo Farm involved Michael Coates (University of Chicago).

items.bewering: Elke nuwe fossiel vertel iets meer oor die lewe van lank gelede.
items.bron: General principle of palaeontology (EBSCO Research Starters 'Fossil record': the record grows and is refined with new finds). Sound as a general statement.

items.bewering: fossielrekord: Al die fossiele wat in 'n plek se rotse bewaar gebly het.
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters and encyclopedia.com: the sum total of fossils preserved in the rock strata. Accurate and simple; it agrees with the study block's wording.

items.bewering: Coelacanth: 'n Groot vis wat diep in die see lewe en baie soos visse in fossiele lyk. Wetenskaplikes het net daardie fossiele geken totdat 'n lewende een in 1938 gevang is.
items.bron: FishBase summary 2063; NHM London; Rhodes University archive 2013 (as for the study block).

items.bewering: dolomiet: 'n Sedimentêre rots wat baie soos kalksteen lyk.
items.bron: Arkansas Geological Survey 'Dolostone'; geology.com 'Dolomite': a carbonate sedimentary rock similar to limestone and often impossible to tell apart from it in the field.

items.bewering: Wêrelderfenisgebied: 'n Plek wat vir die hele wêreld belangrik is, op die amptelike wêreldlys staan en beskerm word.
items.bron: UNESCO 1972 World Heritage Convention, as summarised on whc.unesco.org and in the Scientific American piece on the selection process: places of outstanding universal value on the World Heritage List, which the states parties undertake to protect.

opsomming: All 29 claims checked against sources are confirmed, including the 1938 coelacanth, the extinct coelacanth from Makhanda (Serenichthys), dinosaur bones and trackways inside South Africa, and the Cradle's dolomite caves and World Heritage listing; the only point worth a person's glance is that the Cradle lies mostly in Gauteng and extends a little into North West, which the lesson's 'in Gauteng' does not say but does not contradict.
